newsitem.title: CANADA: Toyota to build new coupe in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to build new coupe in Canada.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp. said on Wednesday it planned to spend $298 million to expand its Cambridge plant to produce a new two-door coupe.
Toyota said the new car would resemble a convertible concept car called the Solara, which was unveiled on Wednesday at the Chicago International Auto Show.
The new coupe will be based on the successful front-wheel drive Camry platform.
"We are pleased and honored to be chosen as the manufacturer of this brand new vehicle," said Andy Watanabe, president of Toyota's Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada Inc.
The capacity at Toyota's facility in Cambridge, 100 km (62.14 miles) southwest of Toronto, will hit 200,000 units a year when the plant is retooled to produce the new coupe starting in 1998.
The Cambridge plant, the only Toyota plant in Canada, opened in 1988, with yearly production of 50,000 Corolla vehicles a year. It produced 97,000 Corollas in 1996.
There has been speculation in the past year that Toyota would build a new vehicle at its Cambridge plant.
